newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Athens Stock Exchange is on a roll: the general price index closed at 1.070 points yesterday, up 2.53 percent, at the end of a week of solid gains. Volume was high at over 13 billion drachmas, the highest of the year so far. Prices have increased 14.6 percent since th beginning of the year and the continually increasing volume of transactions appears to come mainly from confident foreign investors.

--The government appears most likely to cancel the tender for the sale of the Bank of Crete following its consideration of the sole offer from the Bank of Piraeus. Sources at the national economy and finance ministry say the offer did not meet certain guidelines.

--Monday's issue of two-year zero coupons will not carry compound interest, sources at the financial ministry say, which will allow the ministry to reduce the cost without reducing nominal interest rates.
--Tax officials have found a average of 30 tax violations at each firm subjected to snap audits in December. Audits on 5,5000 firms in Athens and rural areas found 147,085 violations.

--The Athens bourse rally is just the beginning of a longer-term climb, ING Barings said yesterday, adding investors should concentrate on blue chips rather than laggards. OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, has seen an increase of 24.55 percent in its share price alone since the beginning of the year.
--Alarm bells have gone off at the finance ministry about the disappointing course of tax revenues in December, due mainly to the farmers' protests and the rescheduling of debts by the ministry.
--The Elefsina Shipyards will receive a three-month stay of sale, a government committee on privatisation decided yesterday. KERDOS

--The bourse's impressive performance has been led by bankers in the public and private sector with the blessing of the government's economic team, sources say. In meetings at the end of 1996, bankers decided on joint action on major portfolios.

--Farmers have decided a return to their protests, beginning January 28, with the occupation of public buildings and banks as well as the occupation of tolls. Road blocks will follow if the government does not satisfy demands.
--The 1996 budget will be out by 90 billion drachmas in primary spending, according to the latest estimates.
--The European Union is threatening recourse to the European Court if the government does not fully liberalise the fuel market.
--The national economy ministry has given an in principle approval to the creation of a free industrial zone in the border-situated Ormenios, Evros region.
--The continuing strike by seamen at all Greek ports may lead to Greek coastal shipping being put out of commission, shipowners warn.
